nodes.title: Spare parts criticality classification for a manufacturing plant
nodes.description: We have 4,000 spare parts with consumption, lead time and cost data. Looking for someone to build a criticality classification (multi-criteria) and suggest stocking policies. Academic background in this topic is a big plus.

demo-10.encaje: Es literalmente el tema de tu tesis: clasificación multicriterio de repuestos y políticas de stock. Pocos postulantes podrán mostrar algo así.
demo-10.riesgo: Plazo de 1–3 meses: acota bien el alcance de la primera entrega.
demo-10.apertura: Classifying 4,000 spare parts by criticality is exactly the problem I worked on in my thesis: I combined k-means clustering with TOPSIS and entropy weights to group parts into families and set (R,S) stocking policies for each. With your consumption, lead-time and cost data I would start by profiling the portfolio and proposing the criteria and weights with you, before building the classification.
demo-10.pregunta: Which criteria matter most to you today: downtime cost, lead time or inventory value?

demo-2.encaje: Weibull, MTBF e intervalos de mantenimiento son tu terreno, y piden alguien que hable español con un equipo en Chile/Perú.
demo-2.riesgo: Piden nivel experto: muestra un ejemplo de ajuste Weibull ya hecho.
demo-2.apertura: With 40 slurry pumps and their failure history, the first step is to check whether failures are wear-out (β > 1) or random, because that decides whether preventive intervals make sense at all. I work with Weibull fitting, MTBF and RCM, and I can deliver the analysis as a Python notebook plus a short report, discussing results with your team in Spanish.
demo-2.pregunta: Do you have censored data (pumps still running), or only failure dates?
